plain: To search a place roughly and rob it

webster.text: To plunder; to pillage completely; to strip by plundering; as, to ransack a house or city.

example.quote: They may, unless the general government be restrained by a bill of rights, or some similar restriction, gc into your cellars and rooms, and search, ransack, and
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 16, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
